text:
landon: FYI apiserver keepalives in eu-west1 are dropping since ~03:40, controller-manager leader flips every ~30s, etcd compaction queue climbing. looks correlated with a GPU autoscaler spike. anyone watching?
mina: saw the same, logs show a bunch of 502s from the apiserver proxied to controllers.
ev an: tagging in. is this the autoscaler that pulled nodes from spot pool B and reattached GPUs?
landon: yes, batch job autoscaler popped a large batch (approx 120 pods) at 03:33, attach storms to GPU pool started then.
devon: NAT allocation on the egress routers in eu-west1 hit a soft limit earlier — proxy was rate-limiting new connections. I see keepalives being reset by the LB.
sre-oncall-bot: alert: apiserver_5xx_rate high (eu-west1) — 02:40-03:55 — pager duty triggered.
mina: controller-manager flips because leader lease renewals time out when apiserver drops. that then churns controllers and increases pressure on etcd. vicious loop.
evan: exact error snippet from apiserver logs: ```E0303 03:41:05.123456 1 handlers.go:210] http2: server sent GOAWAY and is closing the connection```
landon: also seeing KV compaction backlog metric jump to 30k ops. etcd leader CPU spikes ~2x during the attach window.
devon: workaround idea: throttle autoscaler burst and pre-warm SNAT allocations / increase ephemeral ports on the egress proxies. can we throttle the job rollout?
mina: we can toggle autoscaler throttle in the orchestration policy. immediate mitigation: set maxBurst to 10 and add 60s spread.
landon: done — reduced maxBurst, applied a 60s spread via /deployments/autoscaler config. rolling now.
infra-bot: config-change: autoscaler.maxBurst=10 autoscaler.spreadSeconds=60 applied by landon at 03:56
evan: after throttle, apiserver keepalives started recovering at 03:59, leader flips dropped to once every ~10m. etcd compaction growth halted.
mina: long-term we need: (1) SNAT pool sizing tied to expected attach concurrency, (2) autoscaler backpressure for control-plane-sensitive regions, (3) controller-manager backoff on leader churn.
devon: +1 on pre-warm strategy. also consider using a separate attach path for GPU-onboard that avoids hitting the same egress proxies for controlplane nodes.
landon: logging action items to the postmortem doc and opening infra ticket for SNAT sizing + autoscaler config per region.
evan: cost note: pre-warming and larger SNAT pools have a small infra cost but will reduce core downtime and rollout retries. logging estimate in ticket. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
mina: nice work team. followups: postmortem, autoscaler policy change permanent, and implement a canary that simulates attach storms to validate SNAT sizing.
landon: tagging ops-owner in ticket and scheduling a short retro at 11:00. thanks all. :thumbsup:
